newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurds walk out of peace talks after killing.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurds walk out of peace talks after killing.

text.p: A Kurdish group on Tuesday walked out of Western-sponsored talks trying to end rivalry between Iraqi Kurdish factions because of the killing of one of its members.
"On receiving the news of the killing of our colleague...we left the meeting," Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) leading member Sami Abdurrahman told a news conference.

He accused the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) of killing Muhittin Rahim, head of the KDP in the Iraqi town of Halabja. "All indications show the PUK is directly involved and responsible for this act of terror."
The PUK reacted by condemning the accusation.

"While the PUK is condemning any terrorist acts we also condemn KDP's allegations, we call upon the neutral parties to investigate in the KDP's allegations," a statement from the PUK's representative office in Turkey said.
The two groups have met frequently in Ankara since they declared a ceasefire at the end of October after weeks of fighting. The United States, Turkey and Britain are sponsoring the talks.
Abdurrahman did not say when and where the killing happened but said his group would not attend further talks until it was cleared up.
"The KDP will not attend any other meeting of this sort until a thorough investigation is carried out under the sponsorship of the peacemakers and the results are declared," he said.
"We think the KDP is using such pretexts for not committing themselves to the Ankara agreement of October 31," the PUK statement said.

The KDP, led by Massoud Barzani, used Iraqi troops and tanks to take the key city of Arbil from its rival last August. The United States fired missiles at southern Iraq in response to Baghdad's involvement.
